<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/">The compiled-unit cache</a><span class="nv-section-count">12</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">One immutable file addressed by its content and environment, verified whole before a page becomes executable.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file">A compiled unit is one immutable file whose address is its content and its environment</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#an-artifact-is-a-relocatable-object-behind-a-self-describing-header">An artifact is a self-describing header over one relocatable object, and it carries no class metadata</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#the-artifact-cache-is-read-not-mapped">A compiled-unit cache entry is read into memory, never mapped</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#a-warm-hit-skips-codegen-not-the-front-end">A warm hit skips codegen and nothing else, and it must beat the compile it replaces</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#an-artifact-is-verified-whole-before-a-page-is-executable">An artifact is hashed in full where it lies, then placed, relocated and only then made executable</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#the-checksum-proves-integrity-and-ownership-proves-trust">The checksum answers corruption; a cache directory another account can write is refused at startup</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#a-bad-cache-entry-is-a-miss-never-an-error">A bad cache entry is a miss the script never sees, and only a corrupt one is deleted</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#a-writer-publishes-by-one-atomic-rename-and-never-a-lock">A writer publishes by one atomic rename, and a path that already exists wins</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#eviction-rides-the-cold-miss-at-a-probability">Eviction rides the cold miss at a configured probability, and a warm hit pays nothing for it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#nvs-cache-gc-and-clear-are-the-deterministic-escape"><code>nvs cache gc</code> and <code>nvs cache clear</code> are the operator's deterministic alternative to the roll</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#autoload-probes-fold-into-the-cache-key">A unit's cache key covers every autoload path it probed, misses included, and every directory a discovery query listed</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#a-wasm-module-cache-reuses-the-artifact-cache">A compiled extension module is cached in the same store, under the same key, header and verify shape</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/">Single-file builds</a><span class="nv-section-count">15</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A bundle is source appended to a copy of the host binary, found by a footer, carrying a notice generated from the dependency graph.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#nvs-build-compile-appends-the-program-to-a-copy-of-the-host"><code>nvs build --compile</code> appends a program to a copy of the <code>nvs</code> binary, and rebundling is running it again</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#a-bundle-carries-source-not-artifacts">A bundle's payload is source, as a flat file list with no archive and no compression</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#a-bundled-require-resolves-at-build-time">Inside a closed-world target every <code>require</code> resolves at build time, and one that cannot fails the build</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#a-bundle-is-found-by-its-footer-before-argv-is-read">A bundle is recognised by a footer the host reads before it parses one argument</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#build-compile-packages-what-is-on-disk-and-resolves-nothing"><code>nvs build --compile</code> packages what is already resolved on disk and fetches no dependency</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#a-nvsx-dependency-embeds-in-the-same-payload">A <code>.nvsx</code> the program depends on is embedded as one opaque entry of the same flat list</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#a-macos-bundle-is-ad-hoc-signed-at-build">A macOS bundle is ad-hoc signed by the build command; PE and ELF need no step</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#a-build-records-no-timestamp">A build records its target, host, profile, compiler, commit and the commit's own date, and never a build date</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#the-banner-states-the-build"><code>nvs --help</code> opens with the README's own title and the version, commit and commit date of the build answering</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#the-windows-binary-says-what-it-is"><code>nvs.exe</code> carries the logo as its icon and the manifest's facts as its version information, and a debug build carries its own icon</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand">The third-party notice is generated from the dependency graph, fails closed, and is never written by hand</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#the-notice-is-embedded-in-the-binary">The notice and Novis's own license are compiled into the binary from the same tree</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#the-cli-surface-is-novis-own">No flag on <code>nvs</code> is inherited from PHP; <code>-h</code> and <code>-V</code> are the Unix baseline and <code>-o</code> the only short flag Novis declares</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#help-text-speaks-to-its-reader">A doc comment clap renders is written for the person reading <code>--help</code>, and cites nothing they cannot open</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#nvs-info-is-the-one-call"><code>nvs info</code> is the one call for build, host and licensing facts, and the one spelling of it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/">Packages</a><span class="nv-section-count">10</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A package is its digest, reached by an ordinary autoload line, and nothing in one runs before your program does.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-package-name-is-vendor-slash-name">A package name is <code>vendor/name</code>, lowercase ASCII compared exactly, and <code>nvs</code> is reserved for first-party packages</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-package-is-its-digest">A package is an immutable source archive whose identity is its BLAKE3 digest</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#package-toml-is-a-tool-input"><code>package.toml</code> is read by the <code>nvs</code> CLI, never by the runtime and never by name resolution</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-package-file-stays-under-its-declared-prefix">Every file in a fetched package declares a namespace under the prefix its manifest claims, and two packages claiming one prefix is a fetch error naming both</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-fetched-package-is-an-autoload-line">A fetched package is reached by an ordinary <code>autoload</code> line in a committed, generated <code>vendor/packages.nvs</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#nothing-runs-before-the-program">Nothing in a package runs before your program does</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-package-cannot-reach-its-host">A package ships no <code>nvs.toml</code>, and none of its <code>require</code> or <code>autoload</code> paths reaches outside its own directory</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum">Resolution selects the highest minimum any package asked for, and nothing upgrades itself</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#the-lockfile-holds-every-digest"><code>package.lock</code> records every package's digest, a mismatch is a hard error, and <code>--locked</code> fetches nothing the lock does not name</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-git-dependency-is-root-only">A git dependency pins an exact commit, and only the root application may declare one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/">The registry and the version contract</a><span class="nv-section-count">13</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">An append-only transparency log, retraction rather than deletion, and a ladder a dependency break goes down before it is forwarded.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log">The registry publishes an append-only transparency log, and a client verifies inclusion and consistency before using an artifact</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#publishing-never-overwrites"><code>nvs publish</code> uploads a clean-checkout archive, and the registry never overwrites a published <code>name@version</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted">A known-bad version is retracted, never deleted, and <code>nvs audit</code> names the minimum bump that clears it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-breaking-release-is-a-new-name">A package that breaks its API publishes under a new name carrying <code>supersedes</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0">Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated">A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left">One <code>MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH</code> for the whole workspace, and below 1.0 the breaking slot moves left</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot">A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded">A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands">A forced user-facing break survives one minor release as a warning naming its replacement, and is removed in the next major</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-move-proves-two-things">A dependency move never fixes a guard test by editing its threshold, and it regenerates the attribution file in the same commit</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#one-bump-one-commit">Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human">Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/">Extensions</a><span class="nv-section-count">12</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A third-party extension is a sandboxed WebAssembly component: fresh per request, no ambient authority, statically typed at the call.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#an-extension-is-a-sandboxed-wasm-component">A third-party extension is a sandboxed WebAssembly component, never a shared library loaded with <code>dlopen</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#three-tiers">Library and extension code sits at one of three tiers: built-in, sandboxed component, or statically linked native</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#an-nvsx-is-one-file-carrying-its-manifest">A <code>.nvsx</code> is a single WebAssembly component whose manifest is an <code>nvs.manifest</code> custom section</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#an-extension-package-carries-two-payloads">An extension package may carry Novis source beside its <code>.nvsx</code>, under one namespace, and the component's manifest registers exactly one class</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#extension-loading-is-root-controlled">An extension loads only from an <code>[[extension]]</code> entry in the root-owned <code>nvs.toml</code>, pinned by its <code>sha256</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#extension-calls-are-statically-typed">An extension's classes are registered from its manifest at load, and a call into one is type-checked at compile time and emitted as a direct call</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#values-cross-as-handles">A value crosses the guest boundary as a bounds-checked handle, never as a pointer</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#a-fresh-instance-per-request">A guest is instantiated fresh for each request that calls it, so extension state cannot leak between requests</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget">A guest runs under the request's CPU and memory caps, and a runaway guest traps rather than hanging a core</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#a-guest-has-no-ambient-authority">A guest has no ambient authority: WASI is not granted by default, and every host function it receives is capability-checked</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#the-boundary-is-the-cost">An extension call costs a fixed ten-odd nanoseconds over a built-in call, so an extension's API is coarse-grained</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#a-c-dependency-answers-two-questions">A C dependency is admitted under ordinary audit only if attacker-controlled data never reaches it; otherwise it needs an exceptional verification record or is confined to wasm</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/running-as-a-service/">Running as a service</a><span class="nv-section-count">10</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">An operator installs a service from the command line. The installer fails closed, and nothing about it is on the request path.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/running-as-a-service/#pdf-decoding-ships-in-the-image-package">PDF is a decode-only format of <code>nvs/image</code>, in the second wave, and never a member of <code>nvs/pdf</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/running-as-a-service/#a-service-is-one-stored-argv"><code>nvs service</code> is a namespace, and everything after a mandatory <code>--</code> is stored verbatim as the argv the service runs</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/running-as-a-service/#the-installer-is-a-sink">The service installer fails closed: a closed <code>serve</code>/<code>run</code> allowlist, no relative path, no argv without <code>--config</code>, no password on a command line</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/running-as-a-service/#the-argv-lives-in-imagepath">On Windows the argv is encoded into the SCM's one <code>ImagePath</code> string, the binary path is always quoted, and nothing else holds it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/running-as-a-service/#a-service-runs-as-a-virtual-account">A service's default identity is the local system account, and <code>--account</code> names any other, the per-service virtual account included</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/running-as-a-service/#a-service-answers-its-manager">A stop drains, a <code>PARAMCHANGE</code> reloads, and the process's console and its lifecycle records go to the event log</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/running-as-a-service/#the-unit-is-printed-and-install-is-the-opt-in">On Linux <code>nvs service unit</code> prints the systemd unit and touches nothing; writing it is an
